abstract.para: Understand how &systemd; resource control partitions CPUs to isolate real-time workloads.

topic.para: &productname; partitions CPUs with the cpuset controller of the unified cgroups v2 hierarchy, which you manage through &systemd;. You assign CPUs to slices, services and scopes with the AllowedCPUs= property. The setting can be persistent or transient.

A unit can only use the CPUs that its parent slice allows. Therefore, to dedicate CPUs to real-time workloads, restrict the primary system slices (such as system.slice and user.slice) to the remaining CPUs. The affinity of an individual process, set with taskset, is limited in the same way.
For a complete shielding procedure, refer to the article Shielding Linux Resources on &productname;.
